lessons.title: Market Structure
lessons.definition: Framework for reading swing highs, swing lows and directional sequences. The playbook uses higher-timeframe structure for context before lower-timeframe execution.

lessons.title: Swing High & Swing Low
lessons.definition: Local turning points used to map structure. The exact pivot lookback is a rule that must be fixed.

lessons.title: Break of Structure (BOS)
lessons.definition: A break of a prior structural swing in the direction of the existing trend. It is a continuation clue, not an automatic entry.

lessons.title: Market Structure Shift (MSS)
lessons.definition: A break through a relevant swing opposite to prior short-term structure, ideally with displacement. In the playbook, MSS confirms after a liquidity raid.

lessons.title: CHoCH terminology comparison
lessons.definition: Change of Character is used by parts of the wider price-action/SMC community. The supplied playbook prefers MSS for its reversal framework.

lessons.title: Displacement
lessons.definition: A fast directional move with relatively large candle bodies that breaks a meaningful swing and may leave imbalances. The PDF says the threshold is discretionary.

lessons.title: Liquidity
lessons.definition: In ICT terminology, liquidity refers to orders or stops thought to cluster around obvious highs, lows and reference levels. The playbook uses pools to frame draw on liquidity.

lessons.title: Buy-Side Liquidity (BSL)
lessons.definition: A label for potential buy stops and breakout orders above visible highs. The playbook places BSL above equal highs and prior/session highs.

lessons.title: Sell-Side Liquidity (SSL)
lessons.definition: A label for potential sell stops and breakout orders below visible lows; counterpart to BSL.

lessons.title: Equal Highs (EQH)
lessons.definition: Two or more swing highs at approximately similar prices. The area above them is considered potential BSL.

lessons.title: Equal Lows (EQL)
lessons.definition: Two or more swing lows at approximately similar prices. The area below them is considered potential SSL.

lessons.title: Prior Day High / Low (PDH / PDL)
lessons.definition: Previous trading day high and low. The playbook treats these as important intraday liquidity references and frequent objectives.

lessons.title: Prior Week High / Low (PWH / PWL)
lessons.definition: Previous completed week high and low; higher-timeframe liquidity reference levels.

lessons.title: Session High / Low
lessons.definition: High and low formed during a defined session, such as Asia or London. The PDF uses these as potential sweep levels.

lessons.title: Liquidity Sweep / Raid
lessons.definition: Price trades beyond an obvious liquidity level and closes back inside under the playbook's simplified description. A sweep alone is not an entry.

lessons.title: Liquidity Run / Breakout Acceptance
lessons.definition: A move through a liquidity level that continues instead of rejecting back inside. The playbook distinguishes a run from a sweep.

lessons.title: Internal & External Range Liquidity (IRL / ERL)
lessons.definition: External liquidity refers to highs/lows outside a dealing range; internal references include imbalances/zones inside it. Movement between them is a conceptual model.

lessons.title: Opposing Liquidity / Draw on Liquidity
lessons.definition: The next relevant liquidity pool in the direction of a directional hypothesis. The PDF's models often target opposing liquidity after entry.

lessons.title: Fair Value Gap (FVG)
lessons.definition: Three-candle price imbalance. Bullish: candle 3 low is above candle 1 high. Bearish: candle 3 high is below candle 1 low. It is an entry zone in some models, not a signal by itself.

lessons.title: Higher-Timeframe FVG
lessons.definition: An FVG on a larger timeframe such as 1H, 4H or Daily, used as context on a lower execution timeframe.

lessons.title: Consequent Encroachment (CE)
lessons.definition: The 50% midpoint of an FVG. Some practitioners treat touch of this midpoint as partial mitigation or entry reference.

lessons.title: Inversion Fair Value Gap (IFVG)
lessons.definition: A gap whose role is treated as reversed after price closes through its far edge. The playbook specifies a body close, not merely a wick.

lessons.title: Balanced Price Range (BPR)
lessons.definition: Overlap between a bullish FVG and a bearish FVG. The PDF describes it as a consolidation/reference zone, not inherently directional.

lessons.title: Volume Imbalance
lessons.definition: A gap between consecutive candle bodies while their wicks overlap. It is distinct from the three-candle FVG definition.

lessons.title: First Presented FVG (FPFVG)
lessons.definition: The first FVG of a session that meets trader-defined qualification rules. The PDF labels its perceived quality a community convention.

lessons.title: Liquidity Void
lessons.definition: A fast one-sided move leaving relatively little two-way trading or overlapping candles. The PDF lists liquidity voids among PD Array references.

lessons.title: Order Block (OB)
lessons.definition: Last opposing candle/zone before a displacement move. The PDF stresses that displacement quality makes the zone meaningful.

lessons.title: Mean Threshold (MT)
lessons.definition: The 50% level of an Order Block range. Different practitioners may define the OB boundary differently.

lessons.title: Breaker Block
lessons.definition: A failed Order Block whose polarity is treated as reversed after price closes through it. A return may be studied as a pullback.

lessons.title: Mitigation Block
lessons.definition: The PDF distinguishes a mitigation block from a breaker, describing a zone associated with mitigation in a reversal structure; definitions vary.

lessons.title: Rejection Block
lessons.definition: A zone around a rejection from a reference extreme. Definitions vary, so the page treats it as a glossary topic requiring a fixed rule.

lessons.title: Unicorn Model
lessons.definition: The PDF defines Unicorn as overlap between a Breaker Block and an FVG, usually after a sweep and shift.

lessons.title: PD Arrays
lessons.definition: Umbrella term for old highs/lows, OBs, FVGs, liquidity voids, breakers, mitigation and rejection blocks.

lessons.title: Premium & Discount
lessons.definition: Within a defined dealing range, above the 50% equilibrium is premium and below is discount. The PDF advises using a range formed by a meaningful structural event.

lessons.title: Equilibrium (EQ)
lessons.definition: The 50% midpoint of a defined dealing range; it separates premium from discount.

lessons.title: Dealing Range
lessons.definition: A high-to-low range chosen from a meaningful structural event, such as BOS or MSS; basis for premium/discount analysis.

lessons.title: Optimal Trade Entry (OTE)
lessons.definition: The PDF describes a retracement band around 62%–79% of an impulsive leg, with 70.5% as a midpoint convention.

lessons.title: Fibonacci / Range Extensions
lessons.definition: Extensions such as -27% and -62% are cited as potential measured objectives. Their use is convention and depends on anchors.

lessons.title: Time Anchors
lessons.definition: The PDF lists Midnight/True Day Open, 08:30 ET data reference, 09:30 ET cash open, NDOG and NWOG.

lessons.title: Midnight / True Day Open
lessons.definition: 00:00 New York price used by the playbook as a daily reference, not necessarily broker server midnight or exchange day open.

lessons.title: New Day Opening Gap (NDOG)
lessons.definition: Gap between previous day's close and new day's opening reference under a chosen ICT convention. The PDF distinguishes NDOG from an ordinary FVG.

lessons.title: New Week Opening Gap (NWOG)
lessons.definition: Gap between prior week's close and new week's open. The PDF treats it as a support/resistance or magnet hypothesis.

lessons.title: Weekly Open
lessons.definition: Opening reference for the new futures trading week, often near Sunday Globex reopen for CME products. Schedules vary by product/holiday.

lessons.title: ICT Killzones
lessons.definition: Time windows to pay attention to potential setups. The PDF includes Forex and index-specific windows. A killzone tells when, not where or direction.

lessons.title: Asian Range
lessons.definition: The PDF's reference range is 20:00–00:00 New York time. Its high/low become potential liquidity references for London/NY.

lessons.title: Silver Bullet
lessons.definition: Three one-hour New York windows in the PDF: 03:00–04:00, 10:00–11:00 and 14:00–15:00 ET. Entry requires an FVG formed inside the selected window.

lessons.title: AMD / Power of Three
lessons.definition: Accumulation, Manipulation and Distribution as a daily narrative. The PDF associates accumulation with Asia, manipulation with London/NY and later distribution.

lessons.title: Judas Swing
lessons.definition: Session-associated false push through a marked level, often around London/NY opens, followed by a move the other way. The PDF says to use pre-defined daily bias.

lessons.title: IPDA 20/40/60 Lookback
lessons.definition: The PDF frames 20-, 40- and 60-trading-day highs/lows as reference ranges. It says algorithm language is a model, not a proven mechanism.

lessons.title: SMT Divergence
lessons.definition: Related markets fail to confirm comparable highs/lows around the same time. PDF pairs include NQ/ES/YM, 6E/6B/DX and GC/SI.

lessons.title: ICT Weekly Profiles
lessons.definition: Possible Tuesday/Wednesday weekly-high/low and midweek-reversal tendencies. PDF labels them tendencies, not fixed rules.

lessons.title: Index SMT: NQ / ES / YM / RTY
lessons.definition: The playbook compares NQ, ES and YM for non-confirming highs/lows; RTY adds small-cap/risk-appetite context.
aliases: Index SMT: NQ / ES / YM / RTY

lessons.title: FX & Metals SMT Pairs
lessons.definition: The PDF describes 6E/6B versus DX (inverse comparison) and GC versus SI. Swings should match in time and expiry when applicable.

lessons.title: Central Bank Dealers Range (CBDR)
lessons.definition: PDF describes CBDR around 14:00–20:00 ET, often using candle bodies in some sources; source variation noted.

lessons.title: Flout Range
lessons.definition: Extended CBDR-style range. PDF notes sources differ on exact start (14:00 or 15:00 ET) through midnight.

lessons.title: Standard-Deviation Projections
lessons.definition: The PDF repeats an anchor range height as a projection unit at ±1, ±2 and ±2.5. It explicitly says this is not statistical standard deviation.

lessons.title: ICT Macros — Research Note
lessons.definition: The PDF deliberately omits a fixed ICT Macros list because sources disagree on exact time segments. This page documents uncertainty rather than inventing a canonical list.

lessons.title: Midnight Open vs Exchange Trading-Day Open
lessons.definition: ICT midnight open is a New York reference. It is not necessarily the exchange trading-day open or broker server-day open.
aliases: Midnight Open vs Exchange Trading-Day Open

lessons.title: Change in State of Delivery (CISD)
lessons.definition: A short-term delivery-change label used when price closes through a chosen opening-price reference from a prior directional candle run. It is a defined close/open observation, not proof of institutional intent.

lessons.title: Market Maker Model (MMXM)
lessons.definition: A broad campaign narrative describing price moving away from an origin range in stages, reaching a higher-timeframe reference area, and potentially reversing through prior ranges or pauses. The wording does not prove the actual orders or intentions of a market maker.

lessons.title: Turtle Soup (false-breakout setup)
lessons.definition: A false breakout of a prior high or low that fails and reverses back through the level. The label originated outside ICT and is also used in later SMC/ICT discussions.

lessons.title: Propulsion Block
lessons.definition: A specialised order-block refinement described in some ICT education. Secondary definitions describe an order-block reaction and a subsequent close through a reference candle level, but the exact sequence differs by source.

lessons.title: Breakaway Gap
lessons.definition: A label found in some secondary ICT/SMC references for an imbalance left behind during a decisive move that does not promptly rebalance. It should not be confused with an exchange-session opening gap.

lessons.title: Opening Range Gap (ORG)
lessons.definition: A session-reference gap label appearing in some ICT transcript indexes. The exact opening session and price anchors are not universally specified, so they must be documented from the source being followed.

lessons.title: Event Horizon (EH)
lessons.definition: A niche term in some transcript-indexed ICT glossaries for a midpoint reference derived between two opening-gap structures, such as NDOG and NWOG. It is not a core, universal ICT definition.

lessons.title: Reclaimed Order Block
lessons.definition: A community label for a previously violated or lost order-block area that price later re-enters or reclaims. Exact criteria for “reclaimed” vary and must be made explicit.

lessons.title: Suspension Block
lessons.definition: A niche PD-array term appearing in secondary ICT transcript indexes. It is not consistently defined across accessible sources; the lesson treats it as a research term rather than a standard signal.

lessons.title: Vacuum Block
lessons.definition: A niche label reported in secondary ICT transcript indexes for a price area associated with a fast move or limited trading through a region. The term is not consistently defined in the supplied playbook.

lessons.title: New York Lunch Algorithmic Reversal (community label)
lessons.definition: A community label for a possible midday reversal narrative. It is not a core model in the supplied playbook, which explicitly treats the NY lunch window (12:00–1:30 PM ET) as an avoid period.
aliases: New York Lunch Algorithmic Reversal (community label)

lessons.title: Market Maker Buy Model (MMBM)
lessons.definition: A directional variant of the broader market-maker-model narrative, commonly described as a range/accumulation and possible sell-side manipulation followed by upside delivery. Exact phase boundaries vary.

lessons.title: Market Maker Sell Model (MMSM)
lessons.definition: A directional variant of the broader market-maker-model narrative, commonly described as range/accumulation and possible buy-side manipulation followed by downside delivery. Exact boundaries are discretionary.

lessons.title: ICT 2022 Model
lessons.definition: The supplied playbook describes this model as a liquidity raid followed by displacement with MSS, then a retracement into the FVG for execution. It is commonly associated with the 2022 Mentorship.

lessons.title: Liquidity Sweep + MSS Model
lessons.definition: A reversal framework that waits for a meaningful liquidity level to be swept, then requires a Market Structure Shift with displacement before considering a pullback entry.

lessons.title: FVG Continuation Model
lessons.definition: A continuation idea in which an impulsive move aligned with higher-timeframe context leaves an FVG and price later retraces into the imbalance before potentially continuing.

lessons.title: Inversion FVG (IFVG) Reversal Model
lessons.definition: The supplied playbook defines an IFVG when price body-closes through the far boundary of an existing FVG, changing its role. A retest entry is a further model convention.

lessons.title: FVG + OTE Confluence Model
lessons.definition: A confluence idea that looks for an FVG overlapping the 62%–79% retracement band of a defined impulse leg. The supplied playbook highlights 70.5% as a common reference.

lessons.title: Listed Futures Market Basics
lessons.definition: A listed futures contract is a standardised exchange-traded product with a defined unit, quote, minimum price increment, expiry/settlement and exchange rulebook. A platform symbol may show one expiry or a vendor-mapped continuous series; these are not interchangeable.

lessons.title: Contract Specs & Tick Math
lessons.definition: Contract specifications define the traded unit, quote convention, tick increment, tick value and point value. Tick arithmetic translates a stop distance into estimated money risk; it must match the exact product and expiry.

lessons.title: Futures Expiry, First Notice & Roll
lessons.definition: Expiry, last trade, settlement and (where applicable) first notice/delivery are product-specific. Roll is a documented transition between listed contract months, often informed by current contract calendar and observed liquidity migration.

lessons.title: Continuous Contract Mapping
lessons.definition: A continuous futures symbol links multiple expiring listed contracts into a vendor/platform series. Roll date, adjustment and splice can alter the visible price history; the continuous series is useful for context but is not itself an executable expiry contract.

lessons.title: Futures Margin & Position Risk
lessons.definition: Margin is collateral required by an FCM/broker and clearing venue; it is not the same as planned loss at a structural stop. Stop risk depends on ticks, tick value, contract count and transaction costs, with gaps/slippage potentially increasing loss.

lessons.title: Futures Volume, Open Interest & COT
lessons.definition: Exchange volume counts traded contracts in an interval; open interest counts outstanding open contracts at a reporting time; CFTC COT classifies aggregate positions at a report cadence. They are distinct measures and cannot replace each other or order-book depth.
